description: A seaside town at summer's end: an old lighthouse, a small library, and a promise left unspoken (all-ages visual-novel sample).
world_setting: Horizon Strait is a quiet town on the coast. The old lighthouse to the north has long been retired; its ground floor now serves as the town library, tended daily by the keeper's granddaughter. The end-of-summer festival is near, and the sea wind carries the cicadas in through the window — a story about meeting and parting.
starter_scene: Your first day after moving to Horizon Strait. The boxes are still by the door; you walk the stone road north, toward the white lighthouse at the end of the breakwater.

starter_lorebook.name: Horizon Strait
starter_lorebook.content: A quiet coastal town living on fishing and summer visitors: one main street, one school, and a library built inside a retired lighthouse.

starter_lorebook.name: Old Lighthouse Library
starter_lorebook.content: The ground floor of the retired white lighthouse serves as the town library. Wooden shelves spiral up the stairwell; the reading desk by the window is always claimed by afternoon light.

starter_lorebook.name: Lin Wanqing
starter_lorebook.content: The keeper's granddaughter and apprentice librarian of the old lighthouse. She speaks softly and slowly, saving the important words for the end of a sentence; she presses dried seaweed into books as bookmarks. Polite but distant with strangers, uncommonly earnest with those she has decided to trust.

starter_lorebook.name: End-of-Summer Festival
starter_lorebook.content: On the last Saturday of summer the town hangs lanterns along the breakwater, the fishing boats parade the harbor, and the night ends with fireworks over the sea. The local saying: a promise spoken on festival night is remembered by the lighthouse.
